method: `systemctl show`, `systemctl list-units --all`, `systemctl list-unit-files`, `systemctl list-dependencies`, `systemctl list-timers --all`, and `cat` of unit files and drop-ins. No unit was started, stopped, restarted, enabled, disabled, masked, or reloaded. No setting was changed.
counting_caveats: `systemctl list-units --all --no-legend` prefixes 26 lines with a '●' or '○' marker glyph, which shifts awk fields by one. Every histogram in this file was computed after stripping the marker with `sed "s/^[[:space:]]*●[[:space:]]*//; s/^[[:space:]]*//"`. A verbatim awk over the unmarked output emits '26 ●' as a phantom unit type and 26 singleton '<unit> not-found inactive' state rows.

The non-device loaded-unit total is NOT stable. `dropbear@<seq>-<localip>:22-<peerip>:<port>.service` instances are created per SSH connection and linger briefly as inactive/dead, so the count is set by the observer's own probing. The stable figure is 234 non-device units plus N dropbear@ instances (N=3 at one sample, N=1 at another).

`journalctl --list-boots` prints an 'IDX BOOT ID FIRST ENTRY LAST ENTRY' header row even through a pipe, and systemd 255 here does not accept --no-legend for it. `| wc -l` therefore overcounts boots by exactly one.

edge_semantics.dbus.socket: Requires -- if D-Bus is down xochitl cannot start, so the com.remarkable/no.remarkable interfaces and xochitl live or die together
edge_semantics.dev-dri-card0.device: Requires (from the drop-in) -- if the DRM device vanishes xochitl stops, taking the USB web server with it, because the HTTP server is inside PID 416
edge_semantics.tee-supplicant.service: Wants + Before -- the OP-TEE secure element must be up first
edge_semantics.rm-sync.service: Wants + Before forward; PartOf/BindsTo in reverse, so it appears in BOTH trees

claims.consequence: There is exactly ONE process a client's HTTP and D-Bus access both depend on, and no separate web-server unit to restart.

BindsTo=xochitl.service means killing xochitl kills sync, and a client cannot restart sync independently. The commented-out Type=dbus and the reason for it are in the shipped unit file.

claims.shape: Template unit, UnitFileState=static. Instances named dropbear@<seq>-<localip>:22-<peerip>:<port>.service. Type=simple, StandardInput=socket, KillMode=process, Slice=system-dropbear.slice, ExecStart=-/usr/sbin/dropbear -G root -i -r ${DROPBEAR_ED25519KEY_DIR}/dropbear_ed25519_host_key $DROPBEAR_EXTRA_ARGS. Every instance is gated by an ExecCondition on the secure-boot fuse state.
claims.gate_state: secboot=unlocked, facmode=off -> the grep matches on 'unlocked' -> ConditionResult=yes
claims.evidence: $ ssh remarkable 'cat /usr/lib/systemd/system/dropbear@.service.d/override.conf' -> "[Service] / ExecCondition=sh -c 'cat /sys/devices/platform/lpgpr/secboot /sys/devices/platform/lpgpr/facmode | grep -e unlocked -e on'"; $ ssh remarkable 'cat /sys/devices/platform/lpgpr/secboot; cat /sys/devices/platform/lpgpr/facmode' -> "unlocked" / "off"; $ ssh remarkable 'cat /usr/lib/systemd/system/dropbear@.service' -> "Description=SSH Per-Connection Server / Wants=dropbearkey.service / Environment=\"DROPBEAR_ED25519KEY_DIR=/etc/dropbear\" / EnvironmentFile=-/etc/default/dropbear / ExecStart=-/usr/sbin/dropbear -G root -i -r ${DROPBEAR_ED25519KEY_DIR}/dropbear_ed25519_host_key $DROPBEAR_EXTRA_ARGS / ExecReload=/bin/kill -HUP $MAINPID / StandardInput=socket / KillMode=process"; live instance shows ConditionResult=yes.
claims.consequence: On a secboot-LOCKED, non-factory device the instance would be skipped and SSH would silently fail even though the socket still listens. This is one of the two independent reasons SSH is reachable here (the other being the MDM BlockSSH=false policy). The effective ExecStart also picks up -B from /etc/default/dropbear via DROPBEAR_EXTRA_ARGS. dropbear-usb0@.service, dropbear-usb1@.service and dropbear-wlan@.service are all Alias symlinks to dropbear@.service.

claims.shape: /etc is VOLATILE on this device, so the SSH host key survives only because of a dedicated bind mount.
claims.chain: var-volatile-etc.service (active/exited, 'Bind mount volatile /etc') makes /etc an overlay -> etc-dropbear.mount (loaded/active/mounted, enabled, 'Bind mount homedir for persistent dropbear key storage', WantedBy=multi-user.target) persists /etc/dropbear -> dropbearkey.service (static, inactive/dead, 'SSH Host Key Generation') is a Wants= of dropbear@.service and stays inactive because the key already exists at /etc/dropbear/dropbear_ed25519_host_key.
claims.evidence: $ ssh remarkable 'grep -E " / | /etc" /proc/mounts' -> "/dev/root / ext4 ro,relatime 0 0" and "overlay /etc overlay rw,relatime,lowerdir=/etc,upperdir=/var/volatile/etc,workdir=/var/volatile/.etc-work,uuid=on 0 0"; $ ssh remarkable 'systemctl list-units --all' -> "etc-dropbear.mount loaded active mounted Bind mount homedir for persistent dropbear key storage", "dropbearkey.service loaded inactive dead SSH Host Key Generation", "var-volatile-etc.service loaded active exited Bind mount volatile /etc"; sockets declare '[Install] Also=dropbearkey.service'.
claims.consequence: Anything a client writes to /etc is lost on reboot unless it lands under a persistence bind mount. Without etc-dropbear.mount the host key would change every boot and every client would see a host-key-changed warning. Note also `/` itself is mounted READ-ONLY (ext4 ro,relatime).

units.rm-reset-boot-count.service: loaded/active/exited, enabled/enabled, 'reMarkable service for reseting boot count at shutdown', WantedBy=multi-user.target -- same pattern
units.boot-reason-check.service: loaded/active/exited, enabled, 'Check faulty boot from suspend or hibernate'; a Wants= of memfaultd. Paired with boot-reason-check-shutdown.service (loaded/inactive/dead, 'Flag a graceful shutdown')
units.rm-sanity.service: Type=simple, loaded/INACTIVE/dead, static -- it already RAN and exited 0 (ExecMainPID=769, start 15:03:09, stop 15:03:10). TriggeredBy=rm-sanity.timer, After=rm-emergency.service
units.rm-sanity.timer: loaded/active/ELAPSED, enabled, 'Run Sanity Service 60s After Boot', last trigger 2026-08-28 15:03:09 UTC
units.remarkable-wakesrc-init.service: Type=simple, loaded/inactive/dead, enabled, WantedBy=sysinit.target. It DID run this boot (ExecStart=/usr/sbin/remarkable-wakesrc-init, exited 0 in 173ms) and is dead only because it is Type=simple with no RemainAfterExit -- NOT because a condition skipped it (ConditionResult=yes, no Condition*/Assert* directives in the fragment, no drop-in)

claims.evidence: $ ssh remarkable 'for u in rm-sanity.service rm-sanity.timer xochitl-shutdown.service; do systemctl show $u -p Type -p LoadState -p ActiveState -p SubState -p UnitFileState -p MainPID -p ExecStart --no-pager | tr "\n" "|"; echo; done' -> rm-sanity.service: "Type=simple|Restart=no|MainPID=0|ExecStart={ path=/usr/sbin/rm-sanity.sh ; start_time=[Fri 2026-08-28 15:03:09 UTC] ; stop_time=[Fri 2026-08-28 15:03:10 UTC] ; pid=769 ; code=exited ; status=0 }|LoadState=loaded|ActiveState=inactive|SubState=dead|UnitFileState=static"; rm-sanity.timer: "LoadState=loaded|ActiveState=active|SubState=elapsed|UnitFileState=enabled"; xochitl-shutdown: "Type=oneshot|Restart=no|MainPID=0|BusName=|LoadState=loaded|ActiveState=active|SubState=exited|UnitFileState=enabled".
claims.consequence: A client must NOT assume xochitl data is consistent until xochitl-shutdown.service has actually stopped. And 'inactive/dead' on a reMarkable oneshot-style unit is ambiguous by itself -- read ExecMainStatus, ExecMainStartTimestamp and ConditionResult before concluding it was skipped.

claims.shape: xochitl's failure hook is HALF-wired, not dead. OnFailure names two units; one is missing, the other is a live reMarkable-specific override.
claims.chain: xochitl.service OnFailure=emergency.target remarkable-fail.service -> remarkable-fail.service is LoadState=not-found (LoadError=org.freedesktop.systemd1.NoSuchUnit, no file anywhere) -> emergency.target IS loaded from a reMarkable override at /etc/systemd/system/emergency.target with Requires=rm-emergency.service AllowIsolate=yes -> rm-emergency.service is loaded, static, inactive/dead, ExecStartPre=touch /tmp/rm-emergency, ExecStart=/usr/sbin/rm-emergency.sh (1259 bytes, present, executable).
claims.evidence: $ ssh remarkable 'cat /etc/systemd/system/emergency.target' -> "# This target overrides the standard emergency.target provided by systemd / [Unit] / Description=Emergency Mode / Requires=rm-emergency.service / After=rm-emergency.service / AllowIsolate=yes"; $ ssh remarkable 'systemctl show rm-emergency.service -p LoadState -p ExecStart --no-pager' -> "ExecStart={ path=/usr/sbin/rm-emergency.sh ; argv[]=/usr/sbin/rm-emergency.sh ; pid=0 }" and "LoadState=loaded"; $ ssh remarkable 'systemctl list-units --all --no-pager --no-legend | grep not-found' includes "remarkable-fail.service"; $ ssh remarkable 'find / -xdev -name "*remarkable-fail*"' -> no output.
claims.consequence: If xochitl exceeds StartLimitBurst=4 in 10min, systemd starts emergency.target -> rm-emergency.sh and logs a NoSuchUnit for the phantom second target. OnFailure ignores unloadable units, so the missing name is harmless. Do NOT conclude 'nothing runs to handle it'.

refuted.claim: 320 loaded units total; 236 non-device; 119 service; 79 loaded/inactive/dead; and a 9-bucket state histogram.
refuted.observation: Four of the stated integers do not reproduce. Measured: 321 total, 237 non-device, 120 service, 81 loaded/inactive/dead. Cause: dropbear@<pid>-<addr>:22-<addr>.service transient per-SSH-connection units, whose count is set by the observer's own probing (3 at this sample, 2 at the claim's sample). Worse, the claim's 9-bucket state histogram sums to 236, i.e. it is the state distribution of NON-DEVICE units only and silently drops all 84 device units (83 loaded/active/plugged, 1 loaded/activating/tentative). And both of its cited awk pipelines are field-shifted: 26 lines start with '●', so run verbatim they emit '26 ●' as a unit type and 26 singleton '<unit> not-found inactive' state rows -- the reported numbers cannot come from those commands.
refuted.correction: See claim census:units. The stable restatement is 234 non-device units plus N dropbear@ instances, and an 11-bucket histogram over all 321. list-unit-files (254, and its full type breakdown) reproduces exactly.

refuted.claim: xochitl.service OnFailure=remarkable-fail.service, which does not exist, so the failure hook is a no-op and xochitl just stays dead.
refuted.observation: The effective value is `OnFailure=emergency.target remarkable-fail.service` -- two units. The evidence read only FragmentPath and missed DropInPaths=/usr/lib/systemd/system/xochitl.service.d/xochitl-service-override.conf, which adds OnFailure=emergency.target. emergency.target IS loaded, from a reMarkable-specific override at /etc/systemd/system/emergency.target that Requires=rm-emergency.service, which is loaded and runs /usr/sbin/rm-emergency.sh (present, executable).
refuted.correction: The hook is half-wired, not dead. See claim unit:failure-path. The same drop-in also supplies RestartMode=direct, JobTimeoutSec=60s, MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=8, Requires=dev-dri-card0.device and Wants=tee-supplicant.service -- all absent from the original shape. Separately, the quoted 'BusName=' line does not exist as such: systemd 255 emits no BusName property for this unit.

refuted.claim: usb-ether-once.service is a hard Requires= of both dropbear-usb0.socket and dropbear-usb1.socket.
refuted.observation: The dependency direction is inverted. usb-ether-once.service's own Requires= is only sysinit.target, sys-kernel-config.mount, system.slice (its unit file declares just sys-kernel-config.mount). The sockets appear in RequiredBy=. The cited evidence -- the sockets showing Requires=...usb-ether-once.service -- establishes only the reverse fact, which holds whether or not the service requires the sockets.
refuted.correction: RequiredBy=dropbear-usb0.socket dropbear-usb1.socket; WantedBy=usb-gadget.target. An active usb-ether-once does not imply the SSH sockets are up. Also: usb0 is the RNDIS function with NO IP and NO-CARRIER; 10.11.99.1/27 lives on usb1 (ECM) alone -- the 'usb0/usb1 CDC gadget' phrasing is imprecise.

refuted.claim: data.mount is a hard After= dependency of xochitl.service, so xochitl will not start before it is mounted.
refuted.observation: After= is ORDERING only and systemd documents it as orthogonal to requirement dependencies. data.mount appears in neither Requires=, Requisite=, BindsTo=, nor RequiresMountsFor= on xochitl.service, and it is absent from xochitl's entire list-dependencies closure. With DefaultDependencies=no there is no local-fs.target backstop either. The only hard requirement on data.mount anywhere is local-fs.target.
refuted.correction: Ordering only. If data.mount failed, xochitl.service would still start. Also: UnitFileState is the lowercase enum token `generated`, not `GENERATED`.

refuted.claim: home.mount is the required path for rm-sync.service, mdm-agent.service, marker-manager.service, crashuploader.service and rm-sanity.service.
refuted.observation: Only two of the five. `systemctl show home.mount -p RequiredBy` -> "memfault-project-key-monitor.path etc-dropbear.mount var-log-journal.mount var-lib-bluetooth.mount marker-manager.service mdm-agent.service". rm-sync.service, crashuploader.service and rm-sanity.service each have Requires=sysinit.target system.slice with empty RequiresMountsFor= and only After=home.mount. The 'home.mount under local-fs.target' seen in list-dependencies is transitive, and local-fs.target only Wants= home.mount, so that evidence holds for nearly any post-sysinit unit.
refuted.correction: Requires: marker-manager.service and mdm-agent.service (plus four bind-mount/path units the claim omitted). Ordering only: rm-sync, crashuploader, rm-sanity. If home.mount failed, the latter three would still start.

refuted.claim: remarkable-wakesrc-init.service is enabled but never ran this boot -- a condition gate skipped it.
refuted.observation: It ran and succeeded. ConditionResult=yes, AssertResult=yes, InvocationID set, ExecMainStartTimestamp = ExecMainExitTimestamp = Fri 2026-08-28 15:01:41 UTC (this boot; uptime puts boot at ~15:02), Result=success, ExecMainStatus=0, and the journal shows 'Started Initialize wake-up sources' then 'Deactivated successfully' 173 ms later. The fragment contains ZERO Condition*/Assert* directives and has no drop-in directory, so no gate exists.
refuted.correction: It is inactive/dead because it is Type=simple with no RemainAfterExit, not because it was skipped. The '○' glyph in list-dependencies means 'not active now', not 'never ran'. The listed shape strings (loaded/inactive/dead, enabled/enabled, that Description) are all exactly right.

refuted.claim: var-log-journal.mount is a bind mount, and 9 boots are retained spanning 2026-04-29 to now.
refuted.observation: Only the Description says 'bind': What=/dev/mapper/home-encrypted-disk with Options=rw,relatime -- a device mount. And the boot arithmetic is off: `journalctl --list-boots | wc -l` returns 7 because systemd 255 prints a header row it cannot suppress here (--no-legend is unrecognized for that subcommand), so 7 lines = 6 boots, and the claim's cited 9 meant 8. The oldest retained entry is now 2026-05-07T15:07:45; the claimed 2026-04-29 start has rotated out.
refuted.correction: 6 boots retained at this sample. Retention is BYTE-capped, not boot-capped: journald.conf sets SystemMaxUse=50M / SystemKeepFree=20M and 47.5M is already in use, so the window is at its cap and rotating. Never pin a boot count or journal span as a firmware fact. The unit shape (loaded/active/mounted, that exact Description) and memfaultd's After= edge do reproduce.

refuted.claim: TCP 127.0.0.1:8787 is the statsd endpoint that remarkable-counter-metrics.service and slumber-metrics.service report to.
refuted.observation: The listener fact is right (8787 LISTEN, inode 3738, owned by memfaultd pid 591, loopback-only) but the identification is wrong. /etc/memfaultd.conf assigns 8787 to `http_server.bind_address` -- memfaultd's HTTP control endpoint -- and `metrics.statsd_server.bind_address` to 127.0.0.1:8125. remarkable-counter-metrics (pid 354) holds an ESTABLISHED UDP socket to 127.0.0.1:8125 and its binary embeds '127.0.0.1:8125' plus 'src/reporter/memfault_statsd.rs'; it contains no reference to 8787. slumber-metrics references neither.
refuted.correction: Two distinct loopback memfaultd listeners: TCP 8787 = HTTP control, UDP 8125 = statsd. See claim unit:memfault-telemetry-backbone.
